newsitem.title: USA: Anheuser Q1 domestic beer market share up.
newsitem.headline: Anheuser Q1 domestic beer market share up.

text.p: Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc said Wednesday that its domestic beer market share in the first quarter was 45.0 percent of industry shipments, up from 44.6 percent a year ago.
Anheuser said its beer shipments in the first quarter were a record 20.8 million barrels, up 0.3 percent from a year ago.
It said first quarter results were led by continued momentum of its Bud Light brand.
In February, Anheuser said, it raised prices, resulting in a $0.10 to $0.15 per six pack increase to consumers in most states.

"We've seen some increased price discounting in certain markets by our competitors as they try to maintain their market share, and we have followed our policy of meeting competitive prices where necessary," August Busch III, chairman, said in a statement. "Overall, however, our February 1997 price increase has held in most of the country."

Earlier, Anheuser reported first-quarter operating earnings of $258 million, or $0.51 per diluted share versus $242 million or $0.47 per diluted share a year ago. The 1996 results exclude a gain on the sale of the St. Louis Cardinals baseball team. With the gain, 1996 first-quarter net income was $275 million or $0.53 per diluted share.

Led by stronger volume in th United Kingdom, China and South America, Anheuser said its international beer operations experienced volume growth of 31 percent in the 1997 first quarter compared to the same 1996 period.
A $68 million expansion, which is expected to be completed in 1998, will approximately double capacity at the Wuhan brewery in China, bringing it to 2.1 million barrels, Anheuser said.
